CHIEF COMPLAINT
Abnormal lab finding with low hemoglobin.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Stephanie is a 49-year-old female presenting for evaluation of low hemoglobin. Over the past couple of months, she has experienced significant fatigue and dizziness, noting that routine activities such as walking a mile or going to work, which she previously tolerated well, now leave her worn out. She denies blood in stools currently, though she did have blood in stools about three years ago which prompted a colonoscopy at that time. She denies dark, tarry, or black stools. She denies heavy menstrual bleeding. She denies syncope, weight loss, or loss of appetite. She does endorse some dizziness but states it has not led to passing out. Regarding her congestive heart failure, she reports that watching her salt intake has been more of a struggle recently due to traveling. She traveled to Vermont and consumed fast food including two cheeseburgers. She has noticed some swelling in her legs but states it is not extreme. She denies shortness of breath or problems lying flat at night. Regarding her prior kidney stones from a couple of years ago, she denies recent flare-ups, back pain, flank pain, or hematuria.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient endorses dizziness and fatigue. She reports mild nasal congestion attributed to seasonal allergies with changing seasons. She denies fever, chills, sore throat, or cough.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Congestive heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (45%), kidney stones, prior colonoscopy with diverticulosis noted three years ago.

MEDICATIONS
Toprol 50 milligrams daily, lisinopril 10 milligrams daily.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient reports recent travel to Vermont. She acknowledges difficulty with salt restriction in her diet.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Blood pressure and heart rate are normal. General: Well-appearing. Cardiovascular: 3/6 systolic ejection murmur appreciated. Lower extremities: Trace to 1+ pitting edema in ankles bilaterally.

RESULTS
Hemoglobin: 8.2 (low). Echocardiogram from six months ago: Left ventricular ejection fraction 45%, moderate mitral regurgitation.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. New anemia: Anemia profile labs ordered to determine type of anemia. Referral to gastroenterology placed for endoscopy and colonoscopy evaluation.
2. Congestive heart failure with fluid retention: Started lasix 40 milligrams once daily. Continuing toprol 50 milligrams daily and lisinopril 10 milligrams daily. Patient counseled on strict salt restriction. Patient instructed to weigh herself daily and call if weight increases, as may need adjustment of diuretic dosing.
3. Kidney stones: Currently stable. Patient advised to continue watching diet and stay hydrated, though acknowledged difficulty with hydration given diuretic use. Patient to call with any questions or concerns.
